Teri Ann Hourihan

No Labels candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Arizona · Challenger

Licensed professional counselor and behavioral health business owner

Teri Ann Hourihan is a Phoenix licensed professional counselor who has practiced since 2017 and owns a behavioral health company. She won Arizona's first No Labels Party gubernatorial primary in July 2026, defeating Hugh Lytle. Her running mate for lieutenant governor is Angela Harrolle Mohan.

Where Hourihan stands

Affordability and housing
Names affordability as a top priority. Proposes increasing attainable housing, reducing barriers to development, and expanding affordable childcare options.
Taxes
Pledges no tax increases.
Water
Names water security as a priority. Proposes conservation, water recycling and reuse, new water sources, rural groundwater protections, and responsible growth.
Data centers
Supports a temporary moratorium on new large-scale data centers, starting on Day One, while the state sets standards for water, energy, infrastructure, transparency, and accountability.
Debates
Took part in the October 6, 2026 Citizens Clean Elections Commission governor debate with Andy Biggs.

Background

  • Licensed professional counselor since 2017
  • Ph.D., 2018
  • Founder and owner of a behavioral health company (Teri's Health Services, per Herald/Review)
  • Won the 2026 No Labels Party primary for governor of Arizona over Hugh Lytle
  • Former longtime Democrat who briefly registered as a Republican (per Herald/Review)
